newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Looks to cash for direction.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Looks to cash for direction.

text.p: Gas oil swaps drifted sideways in quiet trade late afternoon on Monday as players looked to the cash market for direction, traders said.
"The market is waiting for physical players to come out," one trader said.
March gas oil were last quoted at $26.20/$26.40, down from Friday's $26.60/$26.90, brokers said. April was quoted at $24.70/$24.90, largely unchanged from Friday.
April swaps traded earlier in the day at $24.80 per barrel.
Traders said players are unwilling to take large fresh positions as the market's current strength is primarily due to strong support from one trader.
The local trader had last week bought a total of 890,000-barrels in five cargoes loading in March which led to the widening March/April time spread to about $2.00 per barrel.
The March/April time spread eased slightly to trade at $1.55 per barrel this afternoon on expectation by some that the prompt support may be ending soon.

One trader said regional demand is picking up with enquiries heard from China for March arrival cargoes at around $210 per tonne cost-and-freight basis but sellers said hard pressed to source prompt barrels from Singapore.
The trader said ex-terminals sales in Hong Kong were currently done at about $220 per tonne.
Traders said the East-West arbitrage has closed with the April values now at $14.00 per tonne following an increase in prices in the West.
March fuel oil swaps were quoted at $98.50/$100.00 per tonne, down slightly from Friday's $99.50/$100.50 in quite trade.
